examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Losslessness means joining projections reconstructs exactly the original relation without spurious tuples. Dependency preservation means original FDs can be enforced from projected dependencies without joining. These are separate properties. For a binary decomposition, the common attributes determining either component is a lossless-join criterion under FDs. BCNF decomposition is lossless but can lose preservation; standard 3NF synthesis can preserve dependencies.

**Key relationship:** Binary lossless test: (R1∩R2)→R1 or (R1∩R2)→R2 under F⁺

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Compute component intersection.
2. Test whether it determines one component.
3. Check dependency closure from projected FDs separately.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Lossless joining and dependency preservation are independent goals. For a binary decomposition R1,R2, losslessness follows when their intersection functionally determines one component under F+. Projected dependencies must together imply the original constraints for preservation. 3NF synthesis can ensure both; BCNF decomposition can lose preservation.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
R(A,B,C) has A→B. It decomposes into AB and AC. How many join attributes occur in R1∩R2?

**Answer: 1.** The intersection is {A}, one attribute. A→AB holds by reflexivity and A→B, so the intersection determines AB and the decomposition is lossless. The explicit dependency remains enforceable in AB.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Do not infer losslessness merely because all original attributes appear somewhere. A lossy decomposition can create spurious joined tuples.

A lossless join does not by itself guarantee dependency preservation.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

Binary R→R₁,R₂ is lossless under FDs when their intersection:

- **A.** Determines R₁ or R₂
- **B.** Has the fewest attributes
- **C.** Contains only foreign keys
- **D.** Is empty always

**Answer: A.** The common attributes must functionally determine one whole component, preventing spurious recombination.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Lossless and dependency-preserving differ
- **B.** BCNF decomposition can lose dependency preservation
- **C.** Any decomposition is lossless
- **D.** 3NF synthesis can preserve dependencies

**Answer: A, B, D.** Arbitrary projections may join to extra tuples, so C is false.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

R(A,B,C), A→B, decomposed into AB and AC. Number of attributes in the intersection?



**Answer: 1.** The intersection is {A}, one attribute. Since A→AB, this decomposition is lossless.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2025 CS1 · Q47 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/decomposition?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Lossless decomposition and dependency preservation. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. name determines every attribute of team, so it is a key. The nontrivial dependencies have a superkey determinant, making the original schema BCNF and therefore also 3NF. A,D are false.
2. The projected dependencies make name a key in each two-attribute component, so both are BCNF: B.
3. Their intersection is {name}, which determines both components. The binary lossless-join criterion holds: C. Select **B,C**.

#### GATE 2026 CS1 · Q31 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/decomposition?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Lossless decomposition and dependency preservation. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. The 3NF synthesis algorithm guarantees a lossless, dependency-preserving 3NF decomposition, proving A. Since 3NF implies 2NF and 1NF, such a decomposition also establishes B and disproves D’s impossibility claim.
2. BCNF decomposition can lose dependency preservation; lossless joining and dependency preservation are separate conditions. Thus C is true.
3. Select **A,B,C**.
